questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated (id, title, description, keywords, license)
questions.evidence: id: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; title: 'Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI)'; description: ~1000 char narrative; keywords: 19 terms; license_and_use_terms: detailed CC BY-NC 4.0 + AI-READI Data License block
questions.quality_note: All five mandatory fields present with substantive, meaningful content (100% populated)

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields have meaningful content length
questions.evidence: description field spans lines 10-22 (~1000 chars); motivation captured across purposes (3 entries), tasks (3 entries), addressing_gaps (3 entries), each 200-400+ chars
questions.quality_note: Narrative fields far exceed the 200-char threshold with rich contextual detail

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords describing topic coverage
questions.evidence: 19 unique keywords including 'Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus', 'multimodal dataset', 'harmonized data', 'salutogenesis', 'retinal imaging', 'continuous glucose monitoring', 'triple-balanced sampling', 'health equity', 'Bridge2AI'
questions.quality_note: 19 diverse keywords spanning disease, methodology, modality, and program dimensions

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of files and file type diversity in distribution_formats
questions.evidence: distribution_formats lists DICOM (imaging), CSV (tabular/time-series), mHealth standard (wearable), XML (ECG); source formats .fda, .sdt, .FIT, .csv also documented
questions.quality_note: Four+ distinct standardized output formats reflecting genuine multi-modal data

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or dimensional metadata
questions.evidence: Numeric dimensional metadata throughout: 4,000 participants, 53 mL blood draw, 10-day monitoring periods, CGM every 5 minutes, 12-lead ECG, ~1,000 participants (25%) per subpopulation
questions.quality_note: Rich sample-count and dimensional metadata present, though no byte-level file sizes

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs
questions.evidence: doi: 10.57895/fairhub.2; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; additional Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10642459
questions.quality_note: Multiple persistent identifiers including a dataset DOI

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, or institutional sponsors
questions.evidence: funders: 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program ... grant OT2OD032644 ... Additional support from grants P30DK035816, UL1TR003096, and Research to Prevent Blindness. Total funding in 2022: $5,026,499. Opportunity Number: OTA-21-008. Project dates: September 1, 2022 to August 31, 2025.'
questions.quality_note: Agency, multiple award numbers, funding amount, opportunity number, and dates all present

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.description: Presence of deidentification methods, IRB approvals, or ethical sourcing notes
questions.score_label: IRB approval + deidentification + ethical sourcing details
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews: UW IRB approval number STUDY00016228 with reliance agreements from UAB and UCSD, written informed consent; human_subject_research notes Community Advisory Board of 11 and bioethics guidance; privacy handled via public (de-identified) vs controlled-access tiers segregating zip code, genetics, medical records; discouraged_uses prohibits re-identification
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive: specific IRB numbers, reliance agreements, informed consent, and a concrete de-identification approach via access tiering

questions.name: Access Requirements Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy and license are clearly defined
questions.score_label: License + Data Use Agreement + platform access description
questions.evidence: Public access under CC BY-NC 4.0 with download upon license agreement at FAIRhub; Controlled Access Dataset requires 'a separate data use agreement with the University of Washington as Licensor'; 'Access requirements are being developed by the Data Access Committee'
questions.quality_note: License type, DUA requirement, platform, and governing committee all documented

questions.name: Interoperability and Standardization
questions.description: Presence of standard formats, ontologies, or schema conformance
questions.evidence: preproc:5 'Data mapping to standards': OMOP Common Data Model for clinical data, DICOM for retinal imaging, mHealth standard for wearables, RxNorm codes for medications, ICD-10 codes for diabetes classification
questions.quality_note: Standard formats plus explicit mapping to recognized data models and ontologies

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing libraries or tools used in data preparation
questions.evidence: Extensive instrumentation and software documented: REDCap data management, Dexcom G6 CGM, Garmin VivoSmart 5, MoCA Duo Application, retinal devices (EIDON, Spectralis, Maestro2, Triton, Cirrus 5000, FLIO), Philips Pagewriter TC30; format converters (.fda/.sdt -> DICOM, .FIT -> mHealth)
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive tool/instrument list with manufacturers, but software version numbers and repository/URLs are largely absent

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.description: Description completeness of participant recruitment and data acquisition
questions.score_label: Full recruitment and procedural details included
questions.evidence: collection_mechanisms detail EHR screening (ICD-10 E11.X/R73.09, ages 40+, 2020-2025), wave-based recruitment with REDCap invitations, in-person 2.5-4 hr visits at 3 sites, home-based 10-day wearable monitoring, biospecimen collection/biobanking; enrollment dates (began July 18, 2023, through Nov 30, 2026)
questions.quality_note: Full recruitment pipeline and per-domain acquisition procedures documented

questions.name: Version History Documentation
questions.description: Presence of multiple version records and associated dates
questions.score_label: ≥2 versions with change summaries and release dates
questions.evidence: updates: 'Pilot data released May 2024. Data through July 31, 2024 released November 2024 as v1.0.0. Subsequent versions v2.0.0 and v3.0.0 released with additional participants. Final dataset expected ... by November 2026.'
questions.quality_note: Multiple dated versions (pilot, v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0) with change context

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.description: Presence of formal citations or DOI-linked references
questions.score_label: Multiple references and dataset DOI cross-links
questions.evidence: external_resources cite Protocol Publication BMJ Open (Owsley et al. 2025) DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449, Nature Metabolism Commentary DOI 10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, Zenodo archive DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10642459; dataset DOI 10.57895/fairhub.2
questions.quality_note: Multiple DOI-linked publications plus dataset DOI cross-linking

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity, or subgroup details
questions.evidence: 8 subpopulations with target counts (~1,000 / 25% each) across race/ethnicity (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White) and 4 diabetes-severity strata; inclusion (age 40+, English-speaking) and exclusion (pregnancy, type 1 diabetes) criteria; triple-balanced design explained
questions.quality_note: Detailed demographic stratification with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation
questions.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/2; doi 10.57895/fairhub.2; external_resources include aireadi.org, docs.aireadi.org, bridge2ai.org, NIH RePORTER, Zenodo DOI
questions.quality_note: Multiple persistent, resolvable URLs present

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: Public Access Dataset 'available to the public for download upon agreement with a license' at FAIRhub; Controlled Access via DUA with UW; Data Access Committee governs controlled requests; biorepository requests under defined procedures
questions.quality_note: Fully defined access path across public download and controlled DUA pathways

questions.name: Reusability (License Clarity)
questions.description: License is clearly defined and permits identifiable reuse cases
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: CC BY-NC 4.0 'permits others to distribute, remix, adapt, build upon this work non-commercially ... provided the original work is properly cited'; AI-READI Data License prohibits clinical treatment decisions, re-identification, and sharing with non-licensed parties; links to full CC and AI-READI terms
questions.quality_note: Explicit, granular reuse permissions and prohibitions with links to full terms

questions.name: Data Integrity and Provenance
questions.description: Presence of change logs or provenance tracking
questions.evidence: updates.update_details enumerate dated releases (pilot May 2024, v1.0.0 Nov 2024, v2.0.0/v3.0.0) with version-specific documentation at docs.aireadi.org; harmonization/QC provenance in preprocessing and cleaning strategies (REDCap validation, calibration, coordinator certification)
questions.quality_note: Structured, timestamped version history plus documented processing provenance; no explicit checksums

questions.name: Interlinking Across Platforms
questions.description: Metadata connects dataset records across multiple platforms
questions.evidence: external_resources link FAIRhub, aireadi.org, docs.aireadi.org, Bridge2AI, NIH RePORTER (project 10471118), Zenodo, BMJ Open, and Nature Metabolism
questions.quality_note: Cross-platform links span repository, program, funder, archive, and publications

strengths: Complete structural metadata: all mandatory fields populated with 19 keywords and a rich ~1000-char description
Exemplary funding documentation with agency, multiple grant numbers, funding amount, opportunity number, and project dates
Comprehensive ethics: specific UW IRB number (STUDY00016228), reliance agreements, informed consent, Community Advisory Board, and access-tier de-identification
Strong interoperability via OMOP CDM, DICOM, mHealth, RxNorm, and ICD-10 standardization
Well-documented version history (pilot, v1.0.0, v2.0.0, v3.0.0) and dense cross-platform interlinking (FAIRhub, Bridge2AI, NIH RePORTER, Zenodo, BMJ Open, Nature Metabolism)
weaknesses: Software/instrument list omits version numbers and repository/tool URLs
No byte-level file sizes provided (only sample counts and dimensional metadata)
De-identification described via access tiering but without a named method (e.g., HIPAA Safe Harbor)
No explicit data-integrity checksums or hashes for provenance verification
recommendations: Add version numbers and URLs for software tools (e.g., REDCap version, MoCA Duo App version, conversion utilities)
Include per-file or per-modality size estimates alongside the existing sample-count metadata
State the formal de-identification standard applied to the public dataset (e.g., HIPAA Safe Harbor / Expert Determination)
Publish checksums or a manifest for released versions to strengthen integrity verification
